variants.headline: Looking back: union calls a strike
variants.sub: A strike has been called by a union in the colony.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A union had called a strike in {colony}.

The gazette records the call without presuming its subsequent course. A declared strike and an account of actual work stoppages are not interchangeable notices. The public record should also avoid attributing particular terms to the dispute where those terms have not been supplied as part of the reported event.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We support {target} in this assessment. A call for collective action deserves a fair account, and the existence of conflict does not establish that every accusation against a participant is justified.

variants.headline: Looking back: a call to withhold labour
variants.sub: The colony has a union call for strike action.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: A strike had been called by a union in the colony.

The gazette records the call without presuming its subsequent course. A declared strike and an account of actual work stoppages are not interchangeable notices. The public record should also avoid attributing particular terms to the dispute where those terms have not been supplied as part of the reported event.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We support {target} in this assessment. A call for collective action deserves a fair account, and the existence of conflict does not establish that every accusation against a participant is justified.

variants.headline: Looking back: work becomes the subject of a strike call
variants.sub: A union has called a strike in {colony}.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: The colony had a union call for strike action.

The gazette records the call without presuming its subsequent course. A declared strike and an account of actual work stoppages are not interchangeable notices. The public record should also avoid attributing particular terms to the dispute where those terms have not been supplied as part of the reported event.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We support {target} in this assessment. A call for collective action deserves a fair account, and the existence of conflict does not establish that every accusation against a participant is justified.
